messages:
oncall-bot: 🚨 ALERT: realtime API p99 latency spike detected in region=us-west-2. p99=2.8s (SLO=2.0s). Alert rule `realtime_p99_threshold_v2` fired. Potential customer impact for streaming sessions.
anna.sre: acked. I'm jumping on quick triage. @jay.ops can you please take pager if you're available? :phone:
jay.ops: ack — taking pager. I’ll join the voice bridge if needed. any obvious rollback candidates?
maya.prod: graphs: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/latency/realtime?env=prod&region=us-west-2 — p95 ~620ms, p99 jumped to 2.8s over last 6m. Error rates are flat. Streaming stall metric shows increased chunk-latency and rebuffer events.
anna.sre: good — not an error storm. sounds like tail spikes / KV cache pressure or IO stall. nate, can you confirm most affected model/version?
nate.eng: checking model routing now. Looks like heavy traffic on model_id=mistral-4x-serve-v3 (quantized). 83% of requests hitting dedicated pool gpudyn-5a. CPU on proxy pods is fine, GPU utilization ~95% on several nodes.
liz.cs: any active customer pages? CS reported one complaint of slow replies from EU customer but says degraded in last 10m.
maya.prod: quick query to TSDB:
```
max_over_time(realtime_response_ms_p99{region="us-west-2"}[10m])
```
-> shows a sharp step at ~1792233200. Also observed increased request queueing on the serving runtime: queue_depth spikes concurrent with p99.
anna.sre: immediate mitigations to try (quick checks):
- scale up replica set for gpudyn-5a (add 2x nodes)
- temporarily shift a portion of traffic to eu-west-1 (route-policy=latency-fallback)
- fallback to mistral-4x-serve-v2 (slightly slower quality, lower memory footprint)
- flush KV cache on a subset (can reduce eviction storms)
Can someone run scale and route checks? I will monitor metrics and client impact.
jay.ops: on it — running scaler script now.
```
./infra/scale_pool.sh --pool gpudyn-5a --add 2 --region us-west-2
```
Result: requested 2 nodes, provisioning started (expected 90s).
nate.eng: initiating gradual route shift: 10% traffic to eu-west-1 for streaming endpoint `realtime.v1.stream`.
```
api-routes set --service realtime.v1.stream --traffic 10%:eu-west-1
```
Result: new route policy applied.
maya.prod: monitoring: p99 dipped to 2.2s after shift, queue_depth down ~12% but still above baseline.
anna.sre: good. check KV cache hit-rate on affected pods.
nate.eng: KV hit-rate dropped from 88% -> 62% on two pods before scale. Evictions per minute spiked. I suspect a cold-spot eviction cascade on quantized model causing longer token generation tails.
liz.cs: customer impact: CS ran a quick triage with the EU customer — they saw slow streaming completions but no errors. they appreciate the update.
jay.ops: scale completed, new nodes joined. GPU utilization for pool dropped to ~70% across nodes. p99 now ~1.9s in us-west-2 (below SLO), but stream chunk-latency still shows intermittent spikes.
anna.sre: action items (initial triage):
- (nate) validate KV cache eviction policy; consider raising cache size for gpudyn-5a or sticky shard mapping
- (maya) keep the 10% traffic shift until midnight PST as precautionary lift
- (jay) monitor node health and be ready to roll a targeted restart if a pod shows IO stalls
- (liz) log the customer ticket and inform them SLA note: transient degradation, no error responses
- (oncall-bot) create incident ticket with links -> https://incidents.redwood/1792233445

Can someone confirm they have these? I'll hand off to on-call after 30m if stabilized.
nate.eng: will run a targeted cache-size bump on two canary pods and report results.
maya.prod: FYI added a temporary stream-level timeout clamp to reduce worst-case tail latency for long sessions:
```
service.realtime.stream.timeout_token_ms = 3000
```
This is a stopgap — reduces visible tail but may truncate some legitimate long responses.
liz.cs: informing CS: "We've mitigated the major tail and capacity added; monitoring closely. We'll follow up with detailed RCA if degradation recurs."
anna.sre: thanks all. I'm leaving the bridge but staying on slack watch. Handing over to jay as primary on-call for follow-up and RCA kick-off.
jay.ops: ACK. taking over. I'll collect logs (+core dump check) and start an RCA doc if we see recurrence. will ping if anything changes. :clipboard:
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-1792233445. Severity: S2. Assigned: jay.ops. Links: dashboards + runbook.
anna.sre: closing active paging for now — re-open if p99 rises above 2.0s or error rates increase. :white_check_mark:
